name: Financial Times cryptic crossword, Penguin book 1 No 9

book.title: The Penguin Book of Financial Times Crosswords, volume 1

clue.text: It's instrumental in making union a lot of dollars

blocks.note: to act in concert is to act in union, together
a grand is a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: Someone or something helps bring about a marriage, or a trade union, and a huge sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrumental' reads as 'helpful in bringing about', but here it means literally a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A concert grand is the largest kind of piano, built for performance halls, so it is quite literally an instrument.

clue.text: Chance to start...

blocks.note: first meaning: an opportunity
second meaning: the beginning of something, such as a play or game

explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots tie this clue to the next one, which supplies its partner word for ending.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is both an opportunity that comes up and the first part or beginning of an event.

clue.text: ...and finish at same time as judge

blocks.note: first meaning: to bring something to its end
second meaning: to reach a verdict or infer from evidence

explanation.walkthrough: Read with 2-down, the pair suggests one event that starts and ends together; each clue in fact holds two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To conclude is both to bring to an end and to arrive at a judgement after reasoning.

clue.text: Unwise to make gunners keep. quiet

blocks.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
the hushing sound that asks someone to keep quiet

explanation.surface: Telling artillerymen to stay silent would be a foolish order.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop after 'keep' is a print blemish; the phrase is 'keep quiet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash act is reckless and done without thought, which is what unwise behaviour means.

clue.text: Courageous attendant takes care of shooting

blocks.note: game means plucky, willing to have a go
a keeper looks after or attends to something

explanation.surface: A brave assistant handles the gunfire on a film or battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: On a British country estate this person rears and protects game birds for organised shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: The estate employee who manages birds and land for hunting parties looks after the shoot, so the phrase describes the job.

clue.text: Girl gives pound for record

blocks.note: a girl's name
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A girl pays a pound to buy a gramophone record.
explanation.walkthrough: The singular is rare; most solvers know only the plural annals.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is a yearly chronicle entry, a written account or record of events.

clue.text: Very strong cards it might display

indicators.note: what a set of letters might display is another arrangement of them, not the one printed

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A powerful poker hand is what the cards may reveal.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are severe and forceful ones, so the word means extreme or very strong.

clue.text: Completely secure with impudent girl

blocks.note: to bag something is to secure or capture it
with means together with, and
baggage is an old-fashioned word for a cheeky young woman

explanation.surface: Someone makes an arrangement entirely safe in the company of a cheeky young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave bag and baggage is to leave with all your belongings, so the idiom means totally or entirely.

clue.text: Bore kept in good condition

blocks.note: a well is a shaft bored into the ground
preserved means kept safe or maintained

explanation.surface: A tedious person has been looked after well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a dull person, but it is the noun for a drilled hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well preserved, such as an old house or an older person, has lasted with little sign of decay.

clue.text: Welcome navy gives you and me at gates of hell

blocks.note: ave is Latin for hail, a greeting
RN is the Royal Navy
the pronoun for you and me together

explanation.surface: Sailors greet us as we arrive at the entrance to the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: AVERNUS is a crater lake near Naples which the Romans believed was the entrance to the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman myth the lake was the mouth of the underworld, so it stands for the threshold of Hades.

clue.text: Scotsman before tea has time for film editing

blocks.note: mon is the Scots form of man
T sounds like tea, as in 'suits to a T'
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A Scot finds a moment before his cup of tea to cut a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Montage is the technique of cutting and assembling separate shots into one sequence in cinema.

clue.text: Tempestuous spirit makes a good receptionist, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken out loud rather than spelt

blocks.note: an aerial picks up broadcasts, so a good one gives good reception

explanation.surface: A stormy ghost would make an excellent front-desk worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receptionist' suggests a hotel desk; it is the thing that receives a signal. 'Tempestuous' means 'from The Tempest', Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy sprite who serves Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: Lakelets yield a variety that's bony

indicators.note: a variety is a different form of a thing, so the word supplied is turned into another form

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Little lakes produce a lean breed of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Skeletal describes someone so thin that the frame shows, meaning extremely bony or gaunt.

clue.text: Redskin joins association for developing muscles

definitions.note: a phrase saying what the thing is for, standing in for the noun

blocks.note: a dated, now offensive term for a Native American
a club is an association of members

explanation.surface: A Native American signs up to a body-building society.
explanation.walkthrough: An Indian club is a bottle-shaped wooden club swung in gymnastic exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: These weighted wooden clubs are swung around the body as exercise equipment that strengthens the arms and shoulders.

clue.text: A terrible mess follows a meal

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
dinner is a meal

explanation.surface: Disaster strikes after eating.
explanation.walkthrough: A dog's dinner is British slang for a botched job or an awful mess.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom compares a muddle to the heap of scraps put down for a pet, a shambles.

clue.text: Mark getting film award has to ring off

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so a part goes from the word

blocks.note: the Academy Award statuette
a ring is round like the letter O; this is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A film star wins an award but must cancel a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring off' reads as hanging up the phone; it is the circle-shaped letter coming off the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the lasting mark left on skin after a wound has healed.

clue.text: Celebrated catch made by swimmer

blocks.note: a celebrated person is a star
an angler's catch is fish

explanation.surface: A famous fishing haul landed by an Olympic swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: The starfish is a sea creature that lives in water, and a swimmer is anything that moves through water.

clue.text: Chief mainstay at bridge

blocks.note: first meaning: principal, as in an archenemy or archbishop
second meaning: the curved structure that holds a bridge up

explanation.walkthrough: Bridge looks like the card game, where a chief player might be a mainstay; it is the river crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix or adjective the word means principal, and as a noun it is the curved support spanning a gap.

clue.text: Check with company

blocks.note: con is Latin and Italian for with, as in con brio
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: Verify something with the business.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm a booking or fact is to verify that it is correct, the same as checking it.

clue.text: Points of order

blocks.note: surface reading: formal objections raised about procedure at a meeting
setter's reading: the separate items in a set of instructions or commands

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a fixed term from committee meetings; read word by word it describes the detailed parts of an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Directions are instructions telling someone what to do, the individual points that make up an order.

clue.text: Member of resistance gives work to model

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
a model poses, so is a poser

explanation.surface: A wartime partisan hands a job over to a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' suggests the wartime underground; here it simply means opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone resisting a proposal or regime is one who opposes it, a single person among the opposition.

clue.text: Crew catches fish that's long and skinny

blocks.note: a gang is a crew or team of workers
the ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: A trawler crew lands a lean, elongated fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangling describes a tall, thin, awkwardly loose-limbed person, so it means lanky.

clue.text: Biographer making do with a long sentence

definitions.text: making do with a long sentence

blocks.note: first meaning, playful: someone who writes lives

blocks.clueFragment: making do with a long sentence
blocks.note: second meaning: a prisoner serving a life term

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a writer of wordy prose; the long sentence is a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifer is slang for a convict serving life imprisonment, and jokingly one who writes lives of others.

clue.text: A tearaway with some hesitation becomes more mature

blocks.note: a rip is a reckless, dissolute person, a scamp
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A young hooligan who learns some caution grows up.
explanation.definitionFit: Riper is the comparative of ripe, meaning further developed or more fully grown.

clue.text: Ancient queen accomplished nothing

blocks.note: to have accomplished something is to have done it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An old monarch achieved nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido was the legendary founding queen of Carthage, abandoned by Aeneas in Virgil's epic.

clue.text: I flung a cocktail when paying

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixed drink, so the letters before it are mixed up

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone throws a drink at the bar while settling the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainful employment is work that brings in money, so the word describes something profitable or remunerative.

clue.text: Fashionable children are not yet settled

blocks.note: in means in fashion
issue is a legal word for a person's offspring

explanation.surface: Trendy youngsters have not yet found a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter in issue is under dispute and remains undecided, still open to argument.

clue.text: Capital author takes monks a bunch of comics

blocks.note: Karl Marx wrote Das Kapital, 'Capital'
monks address each other as brothers

explanation.surface: A writer from the capital city gathers monks and a pile of comic books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city or money; it is the title of Marx's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho, Harpo, Chico and their siblings were a family troupe of American comedians in vaudeville and film.
